title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 198
paragraphs: These, then, were the events in Thessaly and Achaia. From there Xerxes proceeded to the Malian land, along a gulf of the sea in which there is an ebb and flow of the tide every day. Around this gulf there is a level space, in parts broad but in other parts very narrow; and lofty, inaccessible mountains surrounding this region enclose the whole Malian land and are called the rocks of Trachis. The first city on this gulf as one comes from Achaia is Antikyra, past which flows the river Spercheios out of the land of the Enianians and into the sea. About twenty furlongs from this river there is another called Dyras, which is said to have sprung up in order to bring aid to Heracles when he was burning. Then again, about twenty furlongs from this, there is another river called Melas.
